# D283 — The descending ranking

**Status:** PRE-REGISTERED. Committed **before the runner exists**. Nothing here is a result.
**Date:** 2026-09-02
**Area:** Strategy research · **personal track**

---

## THIS HYPOTHESIS IS POST-HOC. It was generated by looking at results.

**Read this section before any other.** Every number below that motivates the study was produced by
a completed measurement on the same fixture, and the *direction* being tested was chosen **after**
seeing those numbers. That does not make the study illegitimate. It makes the multiplicity
disclosure load-bearing, and **a record that hides its origin is worthless.**

**The four facts that have to be on the record before the construction is described:**

1. **[D280](D280-the-forecast-precheck.md) ran 165 statistics, 161 of them distinct**, across five
   parts. Under the null the largest of 161 independent `|t|`s has a **median near 2.86** and
   exceeds 3.0 about a third of the time — a figure D280 computed for itself and published in its
   own Multiplicity honesty section. **This study's direction was selected from inside that
   search.**
2. **The descending direction was suggested by D280's sign audit**
   (`scripts/d280_sign_audit.py` → `data/d280_sign_audit.json`) **and by
   [D281](D281-the-unfiltered-ranking.md)'s scored result** (`d485caf`). Both found the **ASCENDING**
   short loses, and both reached it independently — one from money, one from a scored book.
   Descending is the complement of a measured failure, which is the weakest possible provenance a
   hypothesis can have and still be worth testing.
3. **D281's own agent declined to flip and re-run**, in writing, in the record: *"The obvious next
   move — flip the ranking to descending and re-run — is not made here."* **I declined it a second
   time** in the [D282](D282-the-overnight-only-short.md) session, where the same 17.60 bp/night was
   recorded as *"the descending arm is post-hoc and is NOT pre-registered here."*
4. **The principal has now asked for it directly, and that request is the reason this is being
   run.** It is recorded as the *reason*, not as an independent *motivation*. Nothing about being
   asked for a test makes its prior better. What it changes is that the test now gets a
   pre-registration, a ledger and a stop clause instead of being run as a one-line edit to an
   existing script — which is the whole of what [R8](../RULES.md#r8) is for.

**Consequence, stated here and repeated in the Ledger:** the D228 best-of floor computed by this
runner is priced over **this study's own cells only**. **The true multiplicity is larger, because
the direction itself was chosen after 165 statistics**, and no floor computed inside this study can
see that. Any `t`-statistic or percentile reported below must be read against **161 + this study's
count**, not against this study's count alone.

## The measurements that motivate it — already done, read, not redone

`data/d280_sign_audit.json`. It takes the book `top_n` actually selects — **the N LOWEST lagged
`hist_L`**, which is the ascending arm D256, D279 and D281 all traded — and reports what a **SHORT**
of those names **EARNS** against the cross-sectional mean of the same bar, in basis points, at zero
cost, out of sample from 2018-01-01. **POSITIVE bp = the short makes money.**

| universe | score | N | window | **short bp** | t |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| ALL | `h` | 10 | **overnight gap** | **−17.60** | −5.42 |
| ALL | `h` | 25 | **overnight gap** | **−14.64** | −7.18 |
| ALL | `h` | 50 | **overnight gap** | **−10.97** | −7.07 |
| ALL | `h` | 25 | intraday session | +2.66 | +0.71 |
| ALL | `h` | 25 | total (close-to-close) | −9.16 | −2.23 |

**The ascending short loses 11–18 bp every night.** D281 reached the same reading from a scored
book: its unfiltered ascending ranking **subtracts −0.113 to −0.167 gross Sharpe** against a
persistent random control, at all three N.

### THE CENTRAL RISK: SYMMETRY IS ASSUMED, NOT MEASURED

**This is the single most important sentence in the pre-registration.** The audit scored **only the
ascending book**. That the LOWEST tail loses 14.64 bp **does NOT imply the HIGHEST tail gains 14.64
bp.**

**The two tails are DIFFERENT NAMES.** Different volatility, different price, different liquidity,
different borrow. Cross-sectional equity returns are skewed, so the mean of a bottom-N tail and the
mean of a top-N tail are not reflections of each other about the cross-sectional mean; short
interest and borrow cost are not symmetric in the cross-section either; and
[FINDINGS §1b](../FINDINGS.md) records that the variance tax scales with `sigma^2`, so **whichever
tail is more volatile pays more of it regardless of which way the edge points.** A high-`hist_L`
name has, by construction, just accelerated *upward* — a different population from one that has
just accelerated down, in every respect that prices a short.

**Therefore the runner MUST measure the descending book directly, and MUST report the ascending book
beside it at matched N, so the asymmetry becomes a measured quantity rather than an assumption.**
That is an explicit deliverable of this study, and it is reported **in the same basis-point units as
the table above** as well as in scored Sharpe. If the descending arm fails, the asymmetry
measurement is the finding; if it succeeds, the asymmetry measurement is what says by how much the
motivating number over-promised.

## The fixture

`us_shorts_daily_raw.csv.gz` — **1,573 names, 4,137,239 rows, 2010-01-04 → 2026-08-26, RAGGED.**
**562 carry a delisting date (35.7%)**, 122 more collapsed while listed. Loaded through
`RP.load_ragged(B.FIXTURE, B.EVENTS, fee_bps=B.FEE_BPS)` where `B = scripts/run_book_single_names.py`
— per-symbol live windows, **equal weight over LIVE names**, delisting as an exit with no
foreknowledge, no forward-filled prices.

D252's own caveat is carried rather than paraphrased: it *"deliberately contains dead companies and
is still not free of survivorship bias"* — provider coverage records 40–76 delistings a year for
2009–2012 against 700–1,000 after 2016, so **the dead cohort is materially under-sampled early in
the span.** This is the fourth study on this fixture and **it has no untouched cohort left.**

---

## The construction — one change from D281, and it is the sign

```
D279     base = -hold_book(hist_L < 0 & md_L >= 0)   rank the survivors by hist_L ASCENDING
D281     base = -hold_book(scored & warm)            rank ALL of them by hist_L ASCENDING
D283     both populations                            rank by hist_L DESCENDING
```

```
score     hist_L from B.signals_ragged, LAGGED ONE BAR (R9), DESCENDING.
          The most POSITIVE acceleration ranks first.

arm       short the N HIGHEST lagged hist_L names. N in {10, 25, 50}.

universes BOTH, and both are reported:
            ALL   every LIVE, WARM name with a finite (md_L, hist_L) pair —
                  D281's population exactly, no value conditions.
            QUAL  hist_L < 0 & md_L >= 0 — D279's and D256's qualifying set.
                  Descending INSIDE it selects the LEAST negative hist_L.

frozen    5 bp/side, borrow 3%/yr, rf 4%, PPY 252, Impulse 34/9, window 252,
          seed 0, 300 null draws. Nothing is varied. No fourth N.
```

**Both universes are carried because D280 measured the ranking's IC to have OPPOSITE SIGNS in
them** — −0.00524 over all live names against +0.00462 inside the qualifying set — and a
sign-flipped arm therefore has an opposite prior in each. Carrying only one would leave the study
unable to say whether any result is a property of the direction or of the population. **The grid
cost of carrying both is declared in the Ledger and is 18 fresh cells.**

**Implementation reuses `C.top_n` and `C.lag1` unchanged**, with the descending arm obtained as
`C.top_n(base, -hist_L, N)`. `top_n` lags internally and unconditionally, and `lag1(-x) == -lag1(x)`,
so the negation cannot disturb the lag; non-finite scores stay non-finite under negation and still
rank last.

### The lag is the correctness requirement, and it has already killed one result here

**[D279](D279-the-concentrated-short-on-dead-inclusive-names.md)'s first result did not exist.**
`top_n` ranked with `score[:, t]` — `hist_L` from the close of the very bar the position was about
to be paid for — instead of `score[:, t-1]`. Measured, not argued:
`corr(hist_L at t, return at t) = +0.0737` against `corr(hist_L at t-1, return at t) = −0.0103`.
`top25` scored **+2.250 Sharpe unlagged and −0.638 lagged**. **A lagged position built from an
unlagged ranking is still look-ahead, and the base being correctly lagged is what hides it.**

**A fix in a dependency is not a guarantee in a caller.** The runner therefore carries an
independent audit, in the pattern of `audit_lag` in `scripts/run_unfiltered_ranking.py`:

**What it asserts.** (a) `base[:, 0]` is identically zero, i.e. `hold_book` lagged the mask; (b) for
every bar `t` and every N and both directions, the held set is re-derived from `score[:, t-1]` by a
**second implementation that does not call `top_n`** — it partitions the qualifying indices into
finite and non-finite scores, sorts the finite block by the raw score in the stated direction, and
appends the non-finite block in panel order — and is asserted **set-equal** to the book actually
scored. **The first disagreement raises and the run aborts.** The audit reports bars verified and
the mean cross-sectional percentile of the held names in **both** the lagged and the contemporaneous
score. **It is reported with the result whether or not it passes.**

A descending book should sit near percentile **1.0** of the lagged cross-section, where D281's
ascending book sat at **0.0055 / 0.0146 / 0.0299**. If it does not, the direction did not take.

## The controls, and the two known control defects this study must not repeat

| | control | what it matches | known defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`rnd-N`** | N names drawn at random **each bar** | count, bars, N | **churns 6–7× harder** than a ranked book and pays 6–7× the fees. Differs from the treatment in *two* ways |
| **`per-N`** | **persistent** random — draw once, HOLD while the name is still in the base, refill only vacancies | count, bars, N, and *usually* turnover | **NOT turnover-matched on an unfiltered universe** |

`per-N` is `persistent_rnd` copied unchanged from `scripts/d279_turnover_decomposition.py`.

### Defect 1 — `rnd-N` IS ONE RNG DRAW, NOT A DISTRIBUTION

D279's runner and its own decomposition drew different sequences for the same nominal cell and
scored it **−1.528** and **−1.633**. `rotation_nulls` takes 300 draws; hurdle C took **one**, and
its margin moved by up to **0.16 Sharpe on the seed alone.**

**Fix, pre-registered: `rnd-N` is drawn FIVE times per cell** from one seeded generator and reported
as a **distribution** — min, median, max, spread. **Hurdle C is scored against the MEDIAN of the
five**, and the stricter *"beats the MAX of the five"* is computed and reported beside it as **C★**.
Five draws is not 300; **the spread is reported so the reader can see how much of any margin is
seed**, which is the quantity D279 could not report at all. **The five draws are five replicates of
one control, not five hypotheses** — see the Ledger.

### Defect 2 — `per-N` IS NOT TURNOVER-MATCHED ON AN UNFILTERED UNIVERSE

D281 found this in its own results and headed it as its primary design error: `persistent_rnd`
refills only **vacancies**, and on an unfiltered universe there is no qualifying condition to stop
qualifying, so the only vacancy is a delisting. Its turnover collapsed to a **0.002×** ratio against
the ranked book — **a random buy-and-hold basket, not a turnover-matched control.**

**Fix, pre-registered: the turnover ratio of BOTH controls to the treatment is computed and printed
for every cell, on both universes**, and any cell whose `per-N` ratio falls below **0.10×** is
flagged `per_not_turnover_matched` in the artifact and **its `per-N` comparison is reported as a
holding-period comparison rather than a selection comparison.** The QUAL universe should retain
vacancies (D279 measured 0.5–0.7× there) and the ALL universe should not. **The verdict does not
rest on `per-N` alone: `rnd-N` brackets the treatment from the high-turnover side, and a treatment
that loses to both controls on opposite sides of the turnover axis has lost on selection.**

### Every cell is reported NET and GROSS

**GROSS = zero fees, zero borrow, zero rf**, on a rebuilt panel with `cost_fraction` zeroed — the
same construction as `d279_turnover_decomposition.py`. **D279 established that this book loses GROSS
on this fixture**, so costs are not the binding constraint and **the gross number is the informative
one.** A cell that fails gross cannot be rescued by a cost assumption.

---

## The overnight / intraday decomposition, because that is where the motivating signal lives

D280's finding is that the effect is **entirely overnight** and that a wrong-signed intraday move
cancels it, which is why close-to-close read as noise. **This study's arm is a close-to-close daily
book, so it holds the sum of the two**, and reporting only the sum would discard the one thing the
motivating measurement said mattered.

**The runner therefore decomposes each descending book's GROSS P&L into three per-bar series**, on
raw OHLC, over the held positions, pooled over live names exactly as `pooled_returns` does:

```
gap[t]       = open[t]  / close[t-1] - 1     both bars live
intraday[t]  = close[t] / open[t]    - 1
close-to-close[t] = close[t] / close[t-1] - 1
```

Each is reported as an **annualised contribution and a `t`-statistic**, alongside the residual
between raw close-to-close and the dividend-carrying `total_log_returns` the scorer uses — **a short
OWES the dividend**, and D280 measured the ex-date mechanism as real, localised and worth 2–3% of
the overnight IC. **Gap and intraday will not sum exactly to the scored total and the residual is
printed rather than hidden.**

**And the same decomposition is reported in the sign audit's own units** — short bp against the
same bar's cross-sectional mean, per window, **for the DESCENDING and the ASCENDING book at matched
N on both universes.** That table is the asymmetry deliverable, and it is directly comparable to the
motivating table above, cell for cell.

## Hurdles

| | standard |
|---|---|
| **V** | **Positive net CAGR** after fees, financing and borrow |
| **C** | **Beats BOTH controls — the MEDIAN of five `rnd-N` draws, and `per-N` — on Sharpe AND on money, GROSS AND NET.** Four comparisons per control, **eight per cell, all required.** **C★** (beats the *max* of the five `rnd-N` draws on all four legs) reported beside it |
| **F** | **Best-of-K floor** ([D228](D228-mining-the-mined-fixture.md)), **one shared offset vector**, **K = 26** — every book in this study that receives a rotation null |
| **E′** | **Effective independent instruments ≥ 3.0 over the HELD BOOK** — `eff_over_book` from `scripts/d279_fix_eprime.py`, **NOT** `RP.effective_instruments(panel, ...)` — and **≥ 500 pooled trades** |
| **H** | Rotation null. **REPORTED, NOT DECISIVE.** See below |

### E′ is expected to degenerate, and that is declared in advance

`eff_over_book` correlates names on bars where **both were HELD**, with a 250-bar overlap floor. On
a rotating top-N book almost no *pair* clears that floor, so the correlation matrix tends to the
**identity** and E′ degenerates into *"how many names accumulated 250 held bars"* — **a headcount
dressed as a breadth measure.** D279 scored **28.00 on 28 names**; D281 scored **63.00 on 63**.

**If this study's E′ returns approximately N, the runner says so explicitly and the record repeats
it**, because at that point the metric has stopped measuring anything. It is retained only because
it was pre-registered in D279 and dropping a hurdle after seeing what it does to a grid is the move
this programme does not make. **No verdict rests on E′ alone.** Per-symbol P&L concentration is
reported beside every cell as the thing E′ was supposed to guard, with D281's warning carried: on a
book whose scored return is negative, `top_name_share` and the scored cell can carry opposite signs
and **it is not interpretable**.

### Hurdle H is broken on this fixture and carries no verdict

[R7](../RULES.md#r7)'s corollary — *a hurdle that everything clears is not evidence, it is a broken
hurdle.* D279 recorded `S1_short|all` at the **100th percentile on both legs with −0.757 Sharpe and
−2.45% CAGR**. D281 recorded something worse: **a RANDOM control, `hist_L|per50`, cleared H at the
100th / 100th while losing money.** **H is computed, printed, and excluded from `clears_all` in code
before the run.** Verdicts rest on **V, C and F**, with E′ as a disclosed side condition.

## The bar this must clear, in numbers, before the run

**From D281's measured ascending contribution over `per-N`, in GROSS Sharpe** (`data/d281_unfiltered_summary.json`):

| N | ascending, over `per-N` | `per-N` gross Sharpe | **perfect antisymmetry would give** | **needed for zero gross** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | **−0.167** | −0.686 | −0.519 | **+0.686** |
| 25 | **−0.116** | −0.648 | −0.532 | **+0.648** |
| 50 | **−0.113** | −0.523 | −0.410 | **+0.523** |

**Even if the two tails were perfectly antisymmetric — the assumption this study exists to test —
the descending book lands near −0.4 to −0.5 gross Sharpe and fails V by a wide margin.** To reach
**zero** gross at N = 25 the descending ranking must add **+0.648**, which is **5.6× what perfect
antisymmetry delivers** and **3.2× what D279's filtered ascending ranking managed (+0.203)**.

**The Grinold prior agrees.** `IR ≈ IC × sqrt(BR)`. At the ALL-names `IC = −0.00524` — **favourably
signed for a DESCENDING short: high score, low forward return** — and 252 bars/yr × 5.44 effective
instruments ≈ 1,371 independent bets, `sqrt(BR) ≈ 37` and **`IR ≈ +0.19`**, up to +0.3 on the most
generous defensible breadth. **D281 measured the ascending arm at −0.113 to −0.167, so the magnitude
of that prior has already been confirmed once on this fixture with the sign reversed.** It is roughly
**a third of what is needed.**

**So the honest prior, written down before the run: THE DESCENDING BOOK DOES BETTER THAN THE
ASCENDING BOOK AND STILL FAILS V.** If it clears V, the Grinold arithmetic is wrong by more than a
factor of three on this fixture and **that** is the finding, ahead of any cell's CAGR.

## Predictions

| | prediction | direction | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **X1** | **On the ALL universe the descending book beats the ascending book on GROSS Sharpe at all three N**, and beats `per-N` gross by a positive margin at N = 25 | **for** | **high** |
| **X2** | **On the QUAL universe the sign flips and descending LOSES to ascending on GROSS Sharpe at all three N**, because D280 measured the ranking's IC as **+0.00462** inside the qualifying set against −0.00524 outside it | neutral — a test of the *mechanism*, not the arm | **moderate** |
| **X3** | **No cell clears V and no cell reaches positive GROSS Sharpe**, on either universe, at any N. The stop below fires | **AGAINST** | **high** |
| **X4** | **The asymmetry is MATERIAL: the descending book's overnight short bp is smaller in magnitude than the ascending book's at all three N on ALL** — the +14.64 bp/night that symmetry would imply at N = 25 is **not** delivered. And the descending book's gross P&L decomposes with a **positive overnight** component and a **negative intraday** component that cancels most of it | **AGAINST** the assumption the study is built on | **moderate-high** |

**X3 and X4 are declared against the construction and X4 is the load-bearing one**, because it is
the assumption named as this study's central risk. **What would falsify X4:** a descending overnight
short bp at N = 25 of **+14.64 or better** on the ALL universe. That outcome says the two tails
*are* mirror images on this fixture, that the caution above was over-stated, and that a
**separate, separately pre-registered** overnight-only construction would be the thing to price
next — **not something this record would then go on to run.**

**What would falsify X1:** the descending book failing to beat the ascending book at any N. That
says the loss D281 measured is not a property of the *direction* but of *concentration into either
tail* — most likely the `sigma^2` variance tax of [FINDINGS §1b](../FINDINGS.md), which is
direction-blind and taxes whichever tail is more volatile. **That is the second most likely outcome
of this study and it would be a more interesting one than X1 holding.**

## Stop

**If no cell clears V, C and F, the descending ranking is closed.** No fourth N, no alternative
score, no re-cut of the universe, no second population beyond the two declared here, no re-run at a
different seed. **Nothing is tuned after a result is seen.**

**Together with D256, D279 and D281, a failure here closes `hist_L`-ranked directional shorts on the
dead-inclusive daily fixture IN BOTH DIRECTIONS** — the four studies between them will have tested
holding everything that qualifies, the top N of what qualifies, the top N of everything, and now the
**bottom** N of both. **That is the whole of the ranking's usable degrees of freedom on this score.**

**If a cell clears, it is not a book entry.** Under [R8](../RULES.md#r8) admission requires a
pre-registered out-of-sample test and **this fixture has no untouched cohort left** — D246's
reserved wide-universe cohort is a different fixture and is not spent here. **A clearing cell would
buy a pre-registration on another fixture, nothing more**, and the post-hoc provenance recorded at
the top of this file travels with it.

## Ledger

Under [R13](../RULES.md#r13) — scoped to a hypothesis, carried where it shaped the search.

| count | N | why |
|---|---:|---|
| **fresh — descending, 2 universes × 3 N** | **6** | the treatment |
| **fresh — `per-N`, 2 universes × 3 N** | **6** | controls are counted like anything else; D228's floor does not care what a cell was built to prove |
| **fresh — `rnd-N`, 2 universes × 3 N** | **6** | **five draws each; the five are replicates of one control, not five hypotheses**, and the spread is reported |
| **fresh total** | **18** | |
| carried: **D281** | 10 | same fixture, same score, same arm family; this study is its complement |
| carried: **D279** | 20 | same fixture, same arms, same score |
| carried: **D256** | 21 | same fixture, same arms; D279 and D281 carried it for the same reason |
| **TOTAL** | **69** | |

**NOT counted fresh, and why.** The **ascending** cells (2 universes × 3 N) and the two
**unconditional bases** reproduce cells already scored and already counted: `ALL|asc{N}` is D281's
`hist_L|top{N}`, `QUAL|asc{N}` is D279's `S1_short|top{N}`, and the bases are `hist_L|all` and
`S1_short|all`. **They are re-scored here to make the asymmetry a within-run matched comparison, and
the runner asserts they reproduce the published Sharpes to 1e-6.** Re-measuring a counted cell is
not a new look; **failing to check that it reproduces would be a new defect.**

**D282 scores ZERO cells and is NOT carried.** Its own record recommends against running it and
records a fresh count of zero, so there is nothing to inherit.

**AND THE COUNT ABOVE IS NOT THE TRUE MULTIPLICITY.** Under D280's own ledger clause — *"any study
whose candidates, scores or fixtures exist because of these measurements inherits all 161
comparisons"* — **this study inherits them, because the DIRECTION ITSELF was chosen from that
search.** D281 disclosed D280 without carrying the count, which was correct for D281: its
construction (remove the filter/ranking collision) was named in FINDINGS §9 before D280 ran.
**D283's construction has no such independent origin.**

**So the number to read any `t` or percentile in the RESULT against is 161 + 69 = 230, while the
D228 empirical floor the runner computes is over K = 26 books and can only see this study.** The
floor **understates the correction**, by construction, and no arrangement of this study's cells can
fix that. **It is stated here so that it cannot be discovered later.**

**NOT carried:** the single-name **intraday** programme (D264–D278, ~430) — different fixture,
different frequency. The ETF programme's 45,783 is not carried for the reasons R13 already records.

# RESULT — appended 2026-09-02, after the run

**`scripts/run_descending_ranking.py`, seed 0, 300 null draws, 2,769s. Artifact:
`data/d283_descending_summary.json`. Console: `data/d283_run.log`.**

**SURVIVORS: NONE. No cell clears V. No cell clears C. No cell clears F. The stop fires.**

**And the study's central risk was the thing that broke. SYMMETRY DOES NOT HOLD — AND IT FAILS BY
SIGN, NOT BY DEGREE.** The motivating number said the ascending short loses 14.64 bp a night, so a
descending short should gain something like it. **The descending short loses 5.14 bp a night.**
**Both tails lose.** The +14.64 bp this study was asked to go and collect **does not exist**, and
the reason it does not exist is the finding.

## The lag audit — the check D279 failed, run first and reported whether or not it passed

| | |
|---|---:|
| `corr(hist_L at t, return at t)` | **+0.0737** — ranking on this is peeking |
| `corr(hist_L at t-1, return at t)` | **−0.0103** — the tradeable version |
| bars re-derived from `score[:, t-1]` and **matched**, each of 12 books | **3,186 / 3,186** |
| **DESCENDING** held names, mean pctile of the **lagged** score, ALL | **0.9945 · 0.9854 · 0.9701** |
| **ASCENDING** held names, same, ALL | 0.0055 · 0.0146 · 0.0299 |
| DESCENDING, QUAL | 0.9672 · 0.9184 · 0.8500 |
| ASCENDING, QUAL | 0.0328 · 0.0816 · 0.1500 |

**The direction took, and the books are lagged.** `audit_lag` was handed the **raw** `hist_L` and a
direction flag — never the `-hs` that `top_n` was given — so a mis-ordered negation would have
raised. It did not, on any of 38,232 bar-cells. **The audit was separately shown to reject an
unlagged descending book before the run**, so its silence is informative rather than vacuous.

**The ascending percentiles reproduce D281's to four decimals**, which is the first of two
reproductions.

## The grid — every cell NET and GROSS

GROSS is zero fees, zero borrow, zero rf. `dsc` is the treatment; `asc` is D281/D279 reproduced;
`rnd` redraws every bar (draw 0 of five); `per` draws once and holds.

## THE ASYMMETRY — the deliverable, and the study's answer

Short bp against the same bar's cross-section, OOS from 2018-01-01, no costs, **on the books
actually scored above**. **POSITIVE = the short makes money.** `sum` is `asc + dsc`: **perfect
antisymmetry gives zero.**

### The unfiltered universe — both tails lose, at every N, in every window that matters

| N | window | **asc bp** | **dsc bp** | **sum** | dsc / mirror |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | **overnight gap** | **−19.42** | **−9.93** | **−29.36** | **−0.51×** |
| 25 | **overnight gap** | **−14.46** | **−5.14** | **−19.60** | **−0.36×** |
| 50 | **overnight gap** | **−10.17** | **−2.98** | **−13.15** | **−0.29×** |
| 25 | intraday | +3.74 | +0.73 | +4.47 | −0.19× |
| 25 | close-to-close | −8.50 | −3.54 | −12.04 | −0.42× |
| 25 | total (scored) | −8.20 | −3.47 | −11.67 | −0.42× |

**`dsc / mirror` is NEGATIVE in every overnight row.** The descending short does not earn a fraction
of what the ascending short loses — **it loses too, in the same direction.** The pre-registration
asked whether the +14.64 bp would be delivered in full or in part. **It is delivered in neither: the
sign is wrong.**

### Why — the symmetric/antisymmetric split, which is the mechanism

Write `asc = c + d` and `dsc = c − d`, so **`c = (asc + dsc)/2` is the DIRECTION-BLIND cost of
holding a `hist_L` tail at all** and **`d` is the DIRECTIONAL component the ranking is supposed to
buy.** Overnight, book alignment:

| universe | N | **c — common, direction-blind** | **d — directional, favours descending** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **ALL** | 10 | **−14.68** | **+4.75** |
| **ALL** | 25 | **−9.80** | **+4.66** |
| **ALL** | 50 | **−6.58** | **+3.60** |
| **QUAL** | 10 | **−1.91** | **+4.29** |
| **QUAL** | 25 | **−1.17** | **+3.12** |
| **QUAL** | 50 | **−0.30** | **+2.44** |

**The directional component is REAL, correctly signed for a descending short, and stable at +2.4 to
+4.8 bp across both universes and all three N.** It is also **two to three times too small to pay
for the company it keeps on the unfiltered universe**, where selecting *either* tail costs 6.6 to
14.7 bp a night before direction is considered.

**And the mechanism is legible: `hist_L` is signed acceleration, so BOTH tails are large-`|hist_L|`
— which is to say both tails are the volatile names.** [FINDINGS §6](../FINDINGS.md) records
overnight drift as a property of volatility rather than of equities, and a short pays that drift
whichever tail supplies it. **`c` is the volatility-selection tax and it is direction-blind by
construction.**

**The qualifying filter is what removes it.** `hist_L < 0 & md_L >= 0` cuts `c` from −9.80 to −1.17
at N = 25 — **an 88% reduction** — while `d` barely moves. **So D279's and D256's filter, which
D281 diagnosed as spending the signal, turns out to have been doing a second job nobody credited it
with: it was suppressing the volatility-selection tax.** That is the most useful thing this study
found and it was not what it was looking for.

### The motivating measurement is over-lagged by one bar, and this is measured, not asserted

**Added to the runner after the pre-registration was committed and before the run, as a correctness
check. It scores no cell.** `d280_sign_audit.py` lags its score with `C.lag1` — column `t` carries
`hist_L[t-1]` — **and** takes its targets through `nxt`, so column `t` carries bar `t+1`'s return.
The pair is `hist_L[t-1]` against `return[t+1]`. **The book D279, D281 and D283 actually trade pairs
`hist_L[t-1]` against `return[t]`.** Either lag alone is correct; **both together is one bar too
many.**

| ALL, overnight, N = 25 | asc | dsc |
|---|---:|---:|
| **`book` alignment** — what the grid above trades | **−14.46** | **−5.14** |
| `audit` alignment — what the motivating number measured | −12.84 | −5.31 |
| *published `d280_sign_audit` value* | *−14.64* | *not measured* |

**The published −14.64 sits between the two**, because the audit also ranked over `live & finite
score` where this study's base additionally requires warm-up and a finite `md_L`. **The one-bar
discrepancy is worth 1.6 bp at N = 25 and does not change any sign or any verdict here** — but it is
a real defect in a file that motivated two pre-registrations, and **the correctly-aligned number is
the one this record quotes throughout.**

## The overnight / intraday decomposition — and X4's second clause is WRONG

Annualised gross contribution over the full scored span, pooled as `pooled_returns` does, zero cost.
**Zero held name-bars had a missing gap component**, in any cell.

| cell | **overnight** | t | **intraday** | t | close-to-close | total (scored) | div residual |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `ALL\|dsc10` | **−0.29%** | **−4.91** | **+0.10%** | +1.17 | −0.15% | −0.16% | −0.01% |
| `ALL\|dsc25` | **−0.49%** | **−4.77** | **+0.13%** | +0.92 | −0.31% | −0.35% | −0.04% |
| `ALL\|dsc50` | **−0.75%** | **−4.32** | **+0.14%** | +0.58 | −0.56% | −0.64% | −0.08% |
| `ALL\|asc10` | −0.48% | −7.80 | +0.07% | +0.64 | −0.34% | −0.38% | −0.04% |
| `ALL\|asc25` | −0.87% | −7.55 | +0.21% | +1.23 | −0.57% | −0.63% | −0.06% |
| `ALL\|asc50` | −1.29% | −6.53 | +0.37% | +1.31 | −0.84% | −0.92% | −0.08% |
| `QUAL\|dsc25` | **−0.16%** | −3.12 | **−0.04%** | −0.55 | −0.19% | −0.23% | −0.04% |
| `QUAL\|asc25` | −0.38% | −4.38 | +0.14% | +1.15 | −0.22% | −0.25% | −0.04% |

**I predicted the descending book's overnight component would be POSITIVE and its intraday component
NEGATIVE. Both signs are the other way round in every cell.** X4's second clause is **falsified**,
and it is falsified with `t` between −4.32 and −4.91 — this is not a near-miss on a noisy statistic.
**The descending book's single largest loss is overnight**, exactly like the ascending book's, and
its intraday leg is a small positive that fails to cover it.

**D280's structural finding survives with its sign intact — the action is overnight and the intraday
leg opposes it — and only the DIRECTIONAL reading of it was wrong.** The overnight window is where
this book's P&L is decided in both directions. It is simply not a window in which shorting a
`hist_L` tail makes money.

**The dividend residual runs −0.01% to −0.08%/yr**, small and correctly signed for a short that owes
it, and it is charged in the scored total.

## The cross-sectional bp that IS positive, and why it is still not money

**`QUAL|dsc25` and `QUAL|dsc50` post POSITIVE total short bp — +0.57 and +0.86 — and lose money
anyway** (gross CAGR −0.23% and −0.38%). **This is [FINDINGS §1a](../FINDINGS.md)'s identity, in the
only form that matters here:**

> `short bp` is measured **against the cross-sectional mean of the same bar**. It is a
> **dollar-neutral** statistic. **The book is an OUTRIGHT short**, so it earns
> `short bp − (the universe's own mean return)`, and over 2018–2026 that second term is large and
> positive.

**A positive cross-sectional edge is not a positive book, and the gap between them is the market.**
Anyone reading the asymmetry table as a strategy result would be off by the equity risk premium —
which is exactly why every bp in this record sits beside a scored cell rather than alone.

## The contribution — descending minus each control, and minus ascending

`rndMED` is the median of five draws. **D281 measured the ASCENDING contribution over `per-N` at
−0.167 / −0.116 / −0.113 GROSS.**

| universe | N | vs `rndMED` net | **vs `rndMED` GROSS** | vs `per` net | **vs `per` GROSS** | **dsc − asc GROSS** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **ALL** | 10 | +1.024 | **+0.177** | −0.019 | **+0.011** | **+0.457** |
| **ALL** | 25 | +0.905 | **−0.015** | +0.047 | **+0.104** | **+0.285** |
| **ALL** | 50 | +0.950 | **+0.038** | +0.164 | **+0.211** | **+0.109** |
| **QUAL** | 10 | −0.266 | **−0.329** | −1.046 | **−0.241** | **−0.345** |
| **QUAL** | 25 | +0.063 | **−0.111** | −0.790 | **−0.091** | **−0.243** |
| **QUAL** | 50 | +0.173 | **−0.095** | −0.414 | **+0.074** | **−0.122** |

**`dsc − asc GROSS` is positive at every N on ALL and negative at every N on QUAL.** The direction
that helps outside the filter hurts inside it, at comparable magnitude and in the sign D280's two
ICs predict. **That is a clean mechanistic confirmation and it is the strongest thing in this
record other than the asymmetry itself.**

**It is also worth +0.457 Sharpe at the very most, on a book sitting at −0.853.**

## Hurdles

| | outcome |
|---|---|
| **V** | **FAILS in all 26 cells.** Every net CAGR is negative, −0.09% to −9.50% |
| **C** | **FAILS in all six descending cells.** Best case `ALL\|dsc50`: **all four Sharpe legs positive and BOTH money legs negative** |
| **C★** | fails everywhere C fails |
| **F** | **FAILS everywhere.** Floor −0.188; the best cell in the study is −0.508 and is a random control |
| **E′** | passes in 4 of 6 descending cells and **decided nothing** — see the defects |
| **H** | computed, **excluded from every verdict**, and broken again — see the defects |

**`ALL|dsc50` is the near miss and it is worth stating precisely: it beats the median random draw
and the persistent control on Sharpe, gross and net, all four legs — and loses to both on MONEY,
gross and net.** Its net CAGR is −0.77% against `per50`'s −0.58%. **A better Sharpe on a bigger loss
is not a result**, and requiring both legs is what stops it reading as one.

## Verdict against the pre-registered predictions

| | prediction | confidence | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **X1** | descending beats ascending GROSS at all three N on ALL, and beats `per-N` gross at N = 25 | high | **CORRECT** — +0.457 / +0.285 / +0.109, and +0.104 over `per25` |
| **X2** | the sign FLIPS on QUAL and descending LOSES to ascending at all three N | moderate | **CORRECT** — −0.345 / −0.243 / −0.122 |
| **X3** | no cell clears V, none reaches positive GROSS Sharpe | high | **CORRECT** — 26 of 26 negative on both |
| **X4a** | the asymmetry is material; the descending overnight bp comes in below the +14.64 symmetry implies | moderate-high | **CORRECT, and by far more than predicted** — it is **−5.14**, the wrong sign entirely |
| **X4b** | the descending book's gross P&L is positive overnight and negative intraday | moderate-high | **WRONG, sign-inverted in every cell, at t −4.3 to −4.9** |

**Four and a half of five.** **X1 is the first prediction declared FOR a construction to hold
anywhere in the D279–D283 sequence** — and it holds while the construction still fails, which is
what a correctly-scoped prediction is supposed to be able to do.

**X4b is the one that was wrong and it was the one I was most confident about.** The reasoning that
produced it — *"the overnight window is where the ascending short loses, so it is where the
descending short must gain"* — **is the symmetry assumption applied to the decomposition instead of
to the tails, and it failed for exactly the same reason the headline did.** Having named symmetry as
the study's central risk, I then re-assumed it one paragraph later. **The record notes that rather
than presenting X4 as a clean pass.**

## Defects and degeneracies — headed, not buried

### 1. `per-N` IS NOT TURNOVER-MATCHED ON THE UNFILTERED UNIVERSE — again, exactly as flagged

Pre-registered against, flagged automatically, and it fired:

| universe | N | `per` / `dsc` turnover | `rnd` / `dsc` | flag |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| ALL | 10 · 25 · 50 | **0.0016× · 0.0018× · 0.0023×** | 6.15× · 6.86× · 7.31× | **NOT MATCHED** |
| QUAL | 10 · 25 · 50 | **0.121× · 0.145× · 0.197×** | 1.39× · 1.53× · 1.76× | matched |

**D281's 0.002× reproduces to two significant figures**, and the QUAL universe behaves as D279 said
it would because a name can stop qualifying there. **On ALL, the `per-N` comparison is a
holding-period comparison and is reported as one.** The verdict does not rest on it: `rnd-N` churns
6–7× *harder*, `per-N` ~500× *less*, **the descending book sits between them and clears neither on
money.**

### 2. `rnd-N` ON ONE DRAW WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN D279 KNEW

The five-draw spread in GROSS Sharpe:

| cell | min | median | max | **spread** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `ALL\|rnd10` | −0.752 | −0.573 | **−0.204** | **0.548** |
| `ALL\|rnd50` | −0.686 | −0.565 | −0.486 | 0.200 |
| `QUAL\|rnd10` | −0.572 | −0.500 | −0.392 | 0.180 |
| `ALL\|rnd25` | −0.586 | −0.463 | −0.448 | 0.138 |
| `QUAL\|rnd50` | −0.553 | −0.466 | −0.435 | 0.117 |
| `QUAL\|rnd25` | −0.605 | −0.563 | −0.492 | 0.114 |

**D279 estimated the seed's influence at up to 0.16 Sharpe. At N = 10 it is 0.548 — three and a half
times worse.** `ALL|dsc10` beats the median draw by +0.177 gross and **loses to the luckiest of five
by −0.371.** **A single-draw hurdle C at N = 10 could have been reported either way depending on the
seed**, and D279 and D281 both ran exactly that hurdle. **This is the strongest evidence yet that
the fix belongs in every runner that uses a matched-count control, and five draws is the minimum,
not the standard.**

### 3. E′ degenerated in 4 of 6 descending cells and decided nothing

| cell | names held ≥250 bars | E′ | reading |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `ALL\|dsc10` | **2** | **2.00** | identity |
| `ALL\|dsc25` | **60** | **60.00** | **identity — E′ is a headcount** |
| `ALL\|dsc50` | 181 | **179.21** | identity |
| `QUAL\|dsc50` | 118 | **117.80** | identity |
| `QUAL\|dsc10` | 3 | 1.81 | real, and fails |
| `QUAL\|dsc25` | 4 | 2.67 | real, and fails |
| `ALL\|rnd10/25/50` | **0** | **0.00** | a bar-by-bar redraw accumulates 250 held bars on *no* name |

**`ALL|dsc25` scoring exactly 60.00 on 60 names is E′ announcing it has stopped measuring
correlation** — D279 saw 28.00 on 28, D281 63.00 on 63, and this is the third consecutive study in
which it has done so. **Every cell that "passes" E′ fails V, C and F**, and the two cells where E′ is
a real number are the two where it *fails*. **It discriminated nothing, in either direction.**

**`top_name_share` is again not interpretable** and is again not interpreted: it reports +10.4% and
+8.9% on the ALL descending cells and **−3.9% to −10.0% on the QUAL ones**, a negative share of a
negative raw total, which is what D281 said would happen on a losing book.

### 4. Hurdle H is broken for the third consecutive study, and a random control tops it again

| cell | net CAGR | net Sharpe | rotation null | reading |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `ALL\|per25` · `ALL\|per50` | −0.29% · −0.58% | −0.693 · −0.881 | **100.0th / 100.0th** | **RANDOM controls at the ceiling on both legs** |
| `ALL\|all` · `QUAL\|all` | −9.50% · −2.45% | −0.760 · −0.757 | **100.0th / 100.0th** | the two worst books in the study |
| `QUAL\|asc50` | −0.56% | −0.659 | **100.0th / 100.0th** | D279's own cell |
| `QUAL\|rnd50` | −1.03% | −1.463 | 99.7th / 100.0th | random again |
| `ALL\|asc10` | −0.41% | −0.969 | **0.7th / 0.7th** | D281's cell, at the floor of its own null |
| **`ALL\|dsc10`** | −0.19% | −0.527 | **50.0th / 19.0th** | the treatment, indistinguishable from chance |

**Eight of 26 cells clear H and all 26 lose money.** Excluded from `clears_all` in code before the
run, as pre-registered. **The informative line is the last one: the descending book sits at the
50th percentile of a null that randomises the timing of its own positions** — better than the
ascending book's 0.7th, and no better than chance.

## What this closes, and what it does not

> *"If no cell clears V, C and F, the descending ranking is closed. No fourth N, no alternative
> score, no re-cut of the universe, no second population beyond the two declared here, no re-run at
> a different seed."*

**No cell cleared V, C or F. THE DESCENDING RANKING IS CLOSED**, and nothing was tuned after the
result was seen.

**Together with D256, D279 and D281 this closes `hist_L`-ranked directional shorts on the
dead-inclusive daily fixture IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** The four studies tested holding everything that
qualifies, the top N of what qualifies, the top N of everything, and the bottom N of both. **That
exhausts the ranking's usable degrees of freedom on this score, and the fixture has no untouched
cohort left.**

**What is NOT closed, stated so the closure is not read wider than it is:**

1. **The overnight window is not closed and this study did not test it.** D283's arm is a
   close-to-close daily book. **What it establishes about the overnight is that a `hist_L` tail
   short loses there in BOTH directions** — which removes the premise
   [D282](D282-the-overnight-only-short.md) was built on more completely than D282's own correction
   did, and **strengthens D282's recommendation not to run.**
2. **The +2.4 to +4.8 bp directional component is real and is not enough.** It sits against D265's
   10 bp round-trip bar and against a 6.6–14.7 bp direction-blind tail tax on the unfiltered
   universe. **It is a measurement, not a candidate**, and anything built on it needs its own
   pre-registration and inherits this study's ledger plus D280's 161.
3. **The factor-neutral branch of [FINDINGS §9](../FINDINGS.md) remains untouched**, as it has been
   since D256.
4. **The filter's second job is a finding, not a proposal.** That `hist_L < 0 & md_L >= 0` suppresses
   88% of the volatility-selection tax is measured here and is **not** a licence to go looking for a
   better filter on this fixture. That search is what the ledger below prices.

## Ledger, as pre-registered

| count | N |
|---|---:|
| fresh — descending, 2 universes × 3 N | **6** |
| fresh — `per-N`, 2 × 3 | **6** |
| fresh — `rnd-N`, 2 × 3 (five draws each, replicates of one control) | **6** |
| **fresh total** | **18** |
| carried: D281 | 10 |
| carried: D279 | 20 |
| carried: D256 | 21 |
| **TOTAL** | **69** |

**Unchanged from the pre-registration. No cell was added after the run.** The lag audit, the
reproduction check, the asymmetry table, the two alignments, the P&L decomposition, E′ and
`top_name_share` all re-read positions already scored.

**The descriptive statistics ARE larger than the cell count and are declared:** the bp table is a
complete factorial re-read — 2 universes × 3 N × 2 directions × 4 windows × 2 alignments = **96
values, with no selection among them**, plus 48 asymmetry summaries derived from those same 96.
**None scores a cell, none is a candidate, and none is quoted as a best-of** — the factorial is
reported whole precisely so that no cell of it can be a survivor.

**AND THE TRUE MULTIPLICITY REMAINS LARGER THAN 69**, as the pre-registration said before the run:
**the DIRECTION itself was chosen after D280's 161 distinct statistics**, so under D280's own ledger
clause this study inherits them. **Read any `t` or percentile here against 161 + 69 = 230.** The
D228 floor of −0.188 is computed over K = 26 books inside this study and **cannot see that
correction.** It did not need to — nothing came within 0.32 Sharpe of it — **but if anything ever
does on this fixture, the floor it clears will be the wrong one.**
